title: Lesson 5: Building Reusable IP and Productized Offerings
description: The difference between an offer and the intellectual property underneath it, why IP is the asset that compounds, and how to turn a repeatable delivery method into a productized offering the practice owns and can sell again without reinventing the scope.

questions.question: How does intellectual property behave differently from an offer?
options: An offer is priced, while IP is given away with each engagement.
An offer is consumed when sold, while IP is an asset that improves as it is used.
An offer is owned by the client, while IP is owned by the practice.
An offer compounds over time, while IP is spent on a single sale.
questions.explanation: An offer is a one-time transaction, but IP is reused and sharpened with every delivery, so using it lowers cost, raises the ceiling on the work the practice can take, and makes it harder to copy.

questions.question: Which set names the kinds of intellectual property a healthy practice builds?
options: Method, templates, reference architecture, internal tooling, and accumulated findings.
Proposals, invoices, contracts, time sheets, and expense reports.
Demand, competence, repeatability, margin, and utilization.
Discovery, build, review, handover, and support.
questions.explanation: These five are the reusable assets underneath an offer: the way work is done, the starting points for deliverables, the canonical design, the automating tooling, and the record of what worked.

questions.question: What capture discipline turns delivered work into an asset?
options: Writing an annual summary of the practice's strengths.
Reusing client-specific material across engagements to save effort.
Recording the method and know-how while the work happens, in a form others can load and run.
Keeping the method in the heads of the people who did the work.
questions.explanation: Doing good work is not the same as building IP; the work is consumed unless the method and know-how are captured deliberately and made loadable, or they leak away and the practice stays small.
